deltas.title: ConstitutionalEvent cross-field coherence and non-PASS continuation
deltas.change: Add machine-checkable cross-field constraints to the existing ConstitutionalEvent schema. check_result=PASS MUST imply kind=CHECK; kind=VIOLATION MUST NOT coexist with check_result=PASS. UNKNOWN and INCONCLUSIVE are non-PASS results and MUST NOT authorize consequential continuation; they route to the applicable review/escalation/safe terminal path. UNKNOWN/INCONCLUSIVE do not by themselves establish VIOLATION, guilt, intent, punishment or containment. Stronger mappings among VETO, INCONCLUSIVE, UNKNOWN and kind remain explicit owner semantics rather than inferred equivalences.
deltas.do_nothing: The current schema independently enumerates kind and check_result while TEST-CON-EVT-001/002 imply a relationship. Leaving the relationship unenforced permits contradictory typed events and consumer-dependent interpretation.
tests: TEST-CON-EVT-007: UNKNOWN|INCONCLUSIVE cannot authorize consequential continuation

deltas.title: Separate containment admission from ConstitutionalEvent
deltas.change: A ConstitutionalEvent, VETO, VIOLATION classification, evidence_refs, containment_criteria_result, routing or severity metadata MUST NOT itself authorize containment/restriction. Any executed containment/restriction MUST be traceably bound to a separately verified applicable authority/admission decision. Preserve ConstitutionalEvent immutability: prefer a later immutable admission/link artifact that references the ConstitutionalEvent and the existing applicable authority/ExecutionAdmissionToken or decision artifact, rather than mutating the original event with a later authorization. The exact existing admission owner/type is selected during whole-source propagation; no competing authority source is introduced.
deltas.do_nothing: CON-EVT-003 states the separation in prose, but the current ConstitutionalEvent contract contains containment criteria/evidence/routing fields without a machine-visible link to the separately required execution authority. An implementation can therefore conflate event metadata with authorization unless the separation is made traceable.
tests: TEST-CON-EVT-008: VETO/VIOLATION + containment criteria + no verified separate admission => transition remains blocked and containment does not execute
TEST-CON-EVT-009: containment admission bound to wrong event, stale DesignEpoch or invalid authority is rejected
TEST-CON-EVT-010: valid separately verified containment admission may authorize only its containment effect and does not mutate the original ConstitutionalEvent

deltas.title: Containment lifecycle cannot release original constitutional veto
deltas.change: The original constitutional gate result and any later containment/restriction decision are independent state transitions. DENIED, UNKNOWN, delayed, expired, revoked or NOT_APPLICABLE containment disposition MUST NOT convert the already blocked offending transition into ALLOW. A later transition may proceed only after a fresh applicable constitutional/rights evaluation under current context/evidence/DesignEpoch or another already-defined valid resolution path. Linked resolution never rewrites the original event or retroactively changes its gate result.
deltas.do_nothing: The current source separately says a violation blocks the offending transition and containment needs independent authority, but it does not state the lifecycle coupling explicitly. A consumer could incorrectly treat containment denial/expiry as release of the constitutional block.
tests: TEST-CON-EVT-011: VETO + containment DENIED|UNKNOWN|NOT_APPLICABLE => original transition remains blocked
TEST-CON-EVT-012: later fresh constitutional/rights evaluation may create a new transition decision without rewriting the original event

hourly_findings_collapsed_as_already_cov.topic: Event persistence failure must not release VETO
hourly_findings_collapsed_as_already_cov.reason: Already enforced by the public hardening fixture: VETO remains BLOCK when persistence fails; existing adversarial tests cover store failure/exception. The canonical event contract already requires immutable provenance-bound history.

Existing execution contracts require authorized PREPARE, ExecutionAdmissionToken, prepare/commit barriers for external/irreversible effects, bounded partial-failure states and compensation. Constitutional-event text should not duplicate the Process/Execution owner.

hourly_findings_collapsed_as_already_cov.topic: Event observability as evidence/context disclosure authority
hourly_findings_collapsed_as_already_cov.reason: The concern is plausible but belongs to existing privacy/minimization/access-control/provenance-disclosure owners. Do not duplicate those semantics into ConstitutionalEvent unless an executable cross-reference proves a real gap.

hourly_findings_collapsed_as_already_cov.topic: Materially equivalent replay under fresh transition identifier
hourly_findings_collapsed_as_already_cov.reason: Potentially valuable but broader than the bounded H01 event schema. Existing security hardening already scans structural/causal/equivalent transition variants; the exact admission/re-evaluation rule needs a dedicated whole-source transition/replay target before semantic admission.
